text:
Mexico Open: Andrew Novak cruises to title for maiden individual PGA Tour triumph at Vidanta Vallarta
Sunday's final round of PGA Tour's Mexico Open sees USA's Andrew Novak claim title victory, his first individual triumph on PGA Tour; Novak, whose only previous tour victory came at last year's Zurich Classic pairs event alongside Ben Griffin, finished on a tournament record 25-under-par
Monday 2 November 2026 00:25, UK
Andrew Novak bounced back from seeing his six-shot lead halved with three straight birdies to card a two-under 69 and win the Mexico Open by five shots, claiming his first individual PGA Tour title.
Novak staked himself to a big lead with rounds of 61-62 the previous two days, and it was going to take something special to track him down. But with a soft bogey on the 10th hole, his lead was down to three over Steven Fisk and Mexico-born Norwegian Kristoffer Ventura.
And then it was effectively over. Novak hit a greenside bunker shot to four feet on the par-5 12th at Vidanta Vallarta, drove the 13th green to 15 feet for a two-putt birdie, and he ended his decisive run with a 45-foot birdie putt on the 14th.
"That kind of really settled everything," Novak said. "Just happy with how I played today. I thought I grinded it out pretty well."
Fisk and Ventura each closed with a 63, and it was particularly meaningful for Ventura. He was at No. 108 in the FedEx Cup Fall, knowing only the top 100 keep full cards for 2027. The runner-up finish, his best as an individual, moved him to No. 76 and locked up his card.
Mackenzie Hughes of Canada shot 66 and wound up in a tie for fourth when Doug Ghim, playing in the final group, made double bogey on the 18th hole. Hughes moved up to No. 101, a manageable spot with three tournaments remaining.
"Gives me a bit of momentum for the last three," Hughes said. "Obviously, I still know I need more points and I need to keep climbing, but today was a big step in the right direction."
Hughes tied for fourth with Ben Griffin, who was Novak's partner when they won the Zurich Classic of New Orleans last year. Griffin (67) was waiting on the 18th green when Novak finished.
"I loved Zurich and everything about that tournament. That's so fun," Novak said. "But it is nice to have one by myself, too. This is one I've been working for for a while. Obviously not a great season for how I wanted it to go, but this is a nice way to kind of finish."
The outcome was never really in doubt, though Novak must have wondered if anything was going to go his way. On the third hole, the easiest of the par 5s, Novak's second shot plugged into the lip and he could only nudge back into the bunker, leading to par. He missed two other birdie chances from just inside 10 feet on the front nine.
"I played really well on the front and didn't get much out of it," he said.
Novak waited his turn, and three straight birdies was more than enough to send him on his way. He moved from No 89 to No 53 in the FedEx Cup, making him practically a lock to at least be in a pair of $20m (£14m) signature events next year at Pebble Beach and Riviera.
The victory also assures Novak will start the 2028 on the upper Championship Series.
Kihei Akina, the 20-year-old sophomore at Brigham Young University (BYU), closed with a 59 and finished 15th. It was his third top-20 finish on the PGA Tour this year.

digest_he: אנדרו נובאק השלים זכייה ראשונה בקריירה בתואר יחידים במסגרת סבב PGA, לאחר שסיים את אליפות מקסיקו פתוחה בתוצאה של 25 מתחת לתקן. נובאק שמר על הובלתו מתחילת התחרות, על אף שיתרונו צומצם במהלך הסיבוב האחרון, וחתם את הטורניר עם תוצאה של שני חבטות מתחת לתקן ביום ראשון. במקום השני סיימו במשותף סטיבן פיסק וקריסטופר ונטורה, שהצליחו לשפר משמעותית את דירוגם בסבב. עבור ונטורה, מדובר בהישג משמעותי שהבטיח את שמירתו על כרטיס השחקן המלא לעונה הבאה. במקביל, שחקנים נוספים כמו מקנזי יוז ובן גריפין סיימו במקום הרבוד המשותף וצברו נקודות חשובות להמשך העונה. הזכייה מעניקה לנובאק זינוק משמעותי בדירוג הכללי והבטחת השתתפות באירועים המרכזיים בשנה הבאה.
